clue.text: Young man well, shedding last of infection

indicators.note: shedding means casting off, so a letter is taken away from the word for well

parts.note: a spring is a natural well, a source of water

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of the word infection

explanation.surface: A young man is recovering, getting over the tail end of an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes N from 'infection', and 'shedding' removes that N from SPRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is an old-fashioned word for a youth or young fellow, like a young shoot.

clue.text: Such questioning thus by commander having arrested deserter

parts.note: so means thus, in that way

indicators.note: having arrested means the commander holds another piece inside

parts.note: CIC is Commander-in-Chief
a rat is someone who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Questioning by a commander who has caught a deserter.
explanation.walkthrough: CIC is the usual abbreviation for Commander-in-Chief; the questioning is the philosopher's method of probing with questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Socratic questioning is a method of probing enquiry, after the Greek philosopher.

clue.text: Vagabond required to smuggle marble

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, as in gun-running
an agate is a kind of playing marble

explanation.surface: A tramp is needed to sneak in a marble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required to' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Runagate is an archaic word for a wanderer or fugitive, so a vagabond.

clue.text: Spare no effort, like police summoned to disturbance?

definitions.meaning: to take pains or work hard at something
officers called out literally head to a scene of trouble

explanation.surface: Police called out to a fracas really put themselves out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taking pains, and literally describes travelling to some trouble.

clue.text: But would an anteater find its fare so tasty?

definitions.text: But would an anteater find its fare so tasty?

parts.words: But would an anteater find its fare so tasty?
parts.note: anteaters have no teeth, so the word for tasty is read as full of teeth, which ants would hardly be to such a creature

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether ants make a delicious meal for the anteater.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means delicious, but split up it suggests something with teeth in it, which is useless to the toothless anteater.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome is a standard synonym for delicious or appetising food.

clue.text: Stop putting up a bar

indicators.note: in a down clue putting up means reading from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: but means except, as does bar

explanation.surface: Advice to stop setting up a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting up' reverses ABUT as a whole. A stop here is an organ stop, a set of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuba is the name of a powerful reed stop on an organ.

clue.text: Going through old border is daily rip off

indicators.note: going through means one piece passes into the middle of another

parts.note: a verge is a border or edge, as of a road
a daily is a British cleaning lady, also called a char

explanation.surface: A complaint that passing an old border every day is a rip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day; 'is' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip someone off is to charge them too much, swindling them.

clue.text: A ship with a propeller certainly shouldn't be touched

definitions.text: A ship with a propeller certainly shouldn't be touched

parts.words: A ship with a propeller certainly shouldn't be touched
parts.note: touched means mad; a ship's propeller is its screw, which it should not have working free

explanation.surface: A warning that a ship's propeller must never be interfered with.
explanation.walkthrough: A screw is a ship's propeller, and touched means slightly mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be slightly crazy, as is someone touched in the head.

clue.text: Recover after oxygen is given by mouth

indicators.note: after means the recover word follows the oxygen symbol

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
to rally is to recover strength

explanation.surface: A patient recovers after oxygen and medicine taken orally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts RALLY behind O.
explanation.definitionFit: Orally means through the mouth, as medicine is given.

clue.text: Go through brook

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to tolerate, as in brook no argument

explanation.surface: Instructions to walk through a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Endure means both undergo hardship and tolerate, as brook does.

clue.text: He painted the governor of a royal castle

definitions.meaning: John ... was the English landscape painter of The Hay Wain

definitions.text: the governor of a royal castle
definitions.meaning: the keeper or warden of a royal castle was historically given this title

explanation.surface: An artist is said to have been in charge of a royal castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Constable names both the famous English painter and an old title for the warden of a castle.

clue.text: Woman with something to eat

parts.note: Vi is a short woman's name, from Violet
and can mean with, joining one thing to another

explanation.surface: A woman arrives carrying some food.
explanation.definitionFit: A viand is an old word for an item of food, usually used in the plural.

clue.text: Graham Greene's aunt not finally so imposing

indicators.note: not finally tells us the closing letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Aunt Augusta is the title character's aunt in Greene's novel Travels with My Aunt

explanation.surface: A remark that a novelist's famous aunt is less grand than she seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finally' removes the last A from AUGUSTA.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means dignified and majestic, a synonym for imposing.

clue.text: Poor writer's son, one who behaves obsequiously

parts.note: a crawler is a toady who fawns on superiors

explanation.surface: A bad writer has a son who fawns on everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'writer's' stands for 'has', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawler writes untidily or produces poor scribbles, so is a bad writer.

clue.text: Uproot a tree originally protected by some French writer

parts.note: de is French for some, as in de l'eau

indicators.note: protected by means the pieces sit inside the writer's name

parts.note: Jean Racine was a French dramatist

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of the word tree

explanation.surface: Advice to dig up a tree first sheltered by a French author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives T from 'tree'; 'protected by' puts AT inside RACINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deracinate is to pull up by the roots, a literal synonym of uproot.

clue.text: Excess of paint in small hotel by church

indicators.note: in means the paint word goes inside the hotel word

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel or pub
tempera is a kind of paint made with egg yolk
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone complains about too much paint used in a little hotel near a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word; 'by' just sets the church letters beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Intemperance means lack of moderation, especially overindulgence, so excess.

clue.text: Man with a leaning towards monarchic rule?

definitions.text: Man with a leaning towards monarchic rule?

parts.note: Roy is a man's name
a list is a tilt or lean, as a ship lists

explanation.surface: A man who prefers government by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of a supporter of the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist is a supporter of monarchy, someone who favours royal rule.

clue.text: Vessel used in one-day trip that's like an epic journey

indicators.note: used in means the vessel is put into the middle of the other letters
trip suggests stumbling, so the letters of one-day fall out of order

parts.note: SS is steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A ship on a day trip that feels like an epic voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges the letters of one-day to ODYEAN before the vessel goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Odyssean describes a long wandering voyage like that of Odysseus in Homer.

clue.text: Foreign judge restricting local leader's exclusive control?

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: strange can mean foreign or alien

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of local

parts.note: to hold is to judge or consider, as in hold someone responsible

explanation.surface: A foreign judge keeps the local leader under tight control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader's' gives L from 'local', and 'restricting' puts it inside STRANGE to make STRANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranglehold is a total grip on something, so complete and exclusive control.

clue.text: Notes on a Tartini piece — this?

definitions.text: Notes on a Tartini piece — this?

indicators.note: piece signals that a part of the clue's words is taken out on its own

explanation.surface: A question about music by the violinist Tartini.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in 'noteS ON A TArtini', and the whole clue also describes the musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is an instrumental piece; Tartini's Devil's Trill is a famous one.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink provided in buffet?

definitions.meaning: in British slang beer or ale
as a verb, to strike or thump hard

explanation.surface: Booze is served at the buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided in' is a link; buffet is the verb meaning hit, not a meal laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallop is British slang for beer and also means a heavy blow.

clue.text: Speaker introducing satellite's composition

indicators.note: introducing means the speaker comes first, leading into the next piece

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
Io is one of the moons of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A speaker introduces a piece of music about a moon.
explanation.walkthrough: IO is a moon of Jupiter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical composition, often on a sacred theme, for voices and orchestra.

clue.text: Folds in suit, way back

parts.note: a plea is a lawsuit or legal action

indicators.note: back means the street abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A tailor notes the folds in a suit go a certain way at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ST into TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleats are folds pressed into cloth, as in a skirt or trousers.

clue.text: Old conductor eagerly sought after out East

indicators.note: out means the letter for East is removed

parts.note: wooed means courted or pursued eagerly

explanation.surface: A former conductor was much in demand outside the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Wood was the British conductor who founded the Proms.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wood was a famous British conductor of the past, founder of the Proms.

clue.text: Not prepared to have attorney rejected by politician

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the attorney letters are reversed

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney in the US
Lib is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: Someone unprepared has their attorney turned down by a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DA into AD.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad-lib remark is improvised, made without preparation.

clue.text: Express regret, establishing a record in sang-froid

indicators.note: in means the record word goes inside the sang-froid word

parts.note: sang-froid means composure, or poise
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Someone apologises coolly while setting a new record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'establishing' is only a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is to say sorry, which is expressing regret.

clue.text: Fearfully anticipate arrest

definitions.meaning: to dread or anticipate with anxiety, the sense behind apprehensive
to seize or take into custody, as police do a suspect

explanation.surface: Someone dreads being taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both seizing a suspect and anticipating something with anxiety.

clue.text: Where some pupils go, say, having been fed?

indicators.note: say tells us to listen to how the school's name is pronounced

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A question about where schoolchildren go once they have had lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON College is a famous English boarding school; 'say' turns it into a soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: Having been fed means having eaten, the past participle of eat.
